scenes.heading: Build a number from ones
scenes.narration: This little printing press has one stamp in each place. Print a one in the hundreds, tens and ones. The strip reads one hundred and eleven. A number made entirely of ones is called a repunit. If each stamp prints three instead, what number will appear?
scenes.title: Build a number from ones

scenes.heading: Fold matching places together
scenes.narration: Three hundreds, three tens and three ones make three hundred and thirty three. Now fit four stamps. Fold the strip between its middle places. The ends meet, and the two inside places meet. Give each touching pair the same digit. Open the strip. It reads the same forwards and backwards. That is a palindrome.
scenes.title: Fold matching places together

scenes.heading: Lift out the two pairs
scenes.narration: Print two on the outside pair and seven on the inside pair. The result is two thousand seven hundred and seventy two. Can you divide it by eleven without long division? Lift the inside stamps. The outside pair contributes two thousand and two. Put the inside pair on a separate strip. Its value is seven hundred and seventy.
scenes.title: Lift out the two pairs

scenes.heading: Find eleven in both strips
scenes.narration: One thousand and one is eleven times ninety one. The outside pair therefore contributes eleven times one hundred and eighty two. One hundred and ten is eleven times ten. The inside pair therefore contributes eleven times seventy. Add the two quotients. One hundred and eighty two plus seventy is two hundred and fifty two.
scenes.title: Find eleven in both strips

scenes.heading: Will every strip pass?
scenes.narration: Change the outside digit. Its two places still contribute that digit times one thousand and one. Change the inside digit. Its two places still contribute that digit times one hundred and ten. Both contributions are multiples of eleven, whatever digits you choose. Here is a harder order for the press. How many four digit palindromes are multiples of thirty three?
scenes.title: Will every strip pass?

scenes.heading: Check the second factor
scenes.narration: Thirty three is three times eleven. We already have the eleven. For the three, check the digit sum. Each chosen digit appears twice, so the digit sum is twice the sum of our two choices. Doubling cycles the remainders one and two into each other. Only zero stays zero. The two chosen digits must therefore add to a multiple of three.
scenes.title: Check the second factor

scenes.heading: Count the choices on the press
scenes.narration: Sort the inside digits by remainder. Zero, three, six and nine go in the first tray. The other trays have three digits each. Outside digits one, four and seven need the remainder two tray. That gives nine strips. Two, five and eight need the remainder one tray. Nine more. Three, six and nine need the first tray. That gives twelve. The order is filled with thirty different palindromes.
scenes.title: Count the choices on the press

scenes.heading: Test a tempting shortcut
scenes.narration: Could zero be an outside digit as well? Try printing zero, six, six, zero. The leading zero disappears. Six hundred and sixty has only three digits. Keep zero in the inside tray, though. Nine thousand and nine is a valid strip. Next time, pair the matching places, test the remaining condition, and count just the digits your press lets you choose.
scenes.title: Test a tempting shortcut
